question: On each of five frozen J7D geometries, does a cross-round anticommuting second star encounter a nonzero next-star expectation in the actual postselected first-record state?
role: Small exact state-sensitive necessary gate before larger complete-law comparison; no general no-go, caller integration or noisy schedule inference
source_basis: Jing Appendix A.2/A.4 ideal red-X and charge projectors

model.state: The same fixed periodic L=2 108-qubit J6M common +1 star/triangle vacuum orbit, private red-X support, exact ideal projectors and no readout noise
model.first_record: Complete 24-site flux/charge/vacuum first record. For each fixture use the predetermined record with every individually deterministic eligible eigenvalue fixed at its exact value and every individually random eligible eigenvalue +1; fail closed if its exact joint mass is zero
model.second_record: Full actual-residual-sector eligible star block is measured and all its outcomes marginalized; do not substitute a selected-star instrument
model.next_record: After the fixed private later red-X fault, test only the first J7D anticommuting next-star witness, not the complete next public joint law
model.dephasing_identity: For the complete commuting second-star block, nonselective measurement maps a next-star Q to zero when any second star anticommutes with Q on the triangle-vacuum orbit, otherwise leaves Q unchanged. Exact first-postselected baseline mean is 2 P(first,+next)/P(first)-1. This is a one-site necessary influence gate, not a sufficient complete-record TV test
model.uncertainty: Exact rational arithmetic on one fixed finite orbit; five geometries are distinct deterministic fixtures, not independent statistical replicates

matrix.selection: Exactly one frozen structurally open branch and one first witness per topology; no adaptive replacement of first record, witness, history or cap
controls: Recompute full first/second/next actual-sector eligibility and J7D witness from pinned topology
Check exact first mass and one-site next baseline on the complete first projector block
Check dephasing identity directly on two-edge witness by summing both outcomes of its anticommuting second projector
Preserve J7E two-edge complete-law exact TV=0 separately
Pins and frozen caller byte-identical before/after

competing_outcomes.state_sensitive_opening: Any selected witness has nonzero exact baseline mean and an anticommuting second operator, so its marginalized one-site next law changes relative to an unmeasured-second counterfactual; this prioritizes, but does not establish, a matched-history full-law contrast
competing_outcomes.selected_record_null: All five selected-record baseline means are zero despite structural anticommutation; only this one-record/one-site matrix is null and alternate first records or joint correlations remain open
competing_outcomes.censored: Any selected first record has zero mass, an input/source/control drift occurs or a compute cap is reached; do not substitute another record or infer null

acceptance: Six pinned inputs pass before and after
All five frozen fixture/witness branches receive exact positive first-record mass or a declared local censor
Full actual-sector second set is used for the dephasing commutator gate; exact baseline is evaluated before any outcome claim
The two-edge direct projector-sum and J7E null controls hold
No complete next-law, caller integration or stochastic work is claimed
stop_rule: Stop at any pin, geometry, eligibility, first-mass, dephasing-control or budget failure. No adaptive first-record replacement, enlarged matrix, complete-law promotion or noisy sampling in this tick.
